comparison: Both strongly support the transcriptomic findings (C2, C52, C53, C55-C58) showing downregulation of P2RX7/IL-18/IFNG axis in IPF patients. OpenEval provides detailed statistical validation (p=1.245e-7, NES 1.85-1.99, FDR <0.05), while peer reviewers explicitly accept these findings without concerns. Peer result also includes C89 (biological context), which OpenEval addresses separately in R9.

Both strongly support the efficacy data (C59-C63) showing HEI3090 reduces fibrosis. OpenEval details multiple orthogonal measures (Ashcroft score, CD140a+ cells, Sirius Red) with statistical significance. Peer reviewers affirm the data as 'solid' and note the manuscript is 'more convincing' with three orthogonal metrics. Peer result also includes C4 (overarching conclusion), which OpenEval addresses in R7.

Both address genetic validation (C64-C66) but with different confidence levels. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with acknowledgment of complexity requiring careful interpretation. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, identifying a paradox that P2RX7 can be both pro-fibrotic (knockout reduces fibrosis) and anti-fibrotic (activation by HEI3090 reduces fibrosis), requesting additional studies to identify discrete phases.

Both support the immune modulation findings (C67-C76). OpenEval provides detailed flow cytometry validation with specific p-values and sample sizes. Peer reviewers accept the findings on inflammatory macrophages, IL-17A reduction, and cytokine changes. Peer result also includes C5-C7 (mechanistic conclusions), which OpenEval addresses in R7.

Both support the adoptive transfer experiments (C77-C81) demonstrating the P2RX7-NLRP3-IL-18 pathway requirement in immune cells. OpenEval describes the experiments as 'elegant' with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers accept the conclusion that HEI3090 enhances IL-18 production through this axis. Peer result also includes C84 (mechanistic pathway), which OpenEval addresses in R7.

Both support the selectivity for IL-18 over IL-1β (C82-C83). OpenEval notes this strengthens mechanistic understanding and is consistent with prior characterization. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this finding as part of the mechanistic specificity without challenge.

Both address HEI3090's mechanism of action (C50-C51) but with different confidence levels. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on prior characterization and current confirmation, noting the molecular mechanism of selectivity requires further investigation. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, requesting additional validation including thermal proteome profiling, direct binding experiments, and orthogonal validation with another P2RX7 modulator or recombinant IL-18.

Both address safety/side effects (C123). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but acknowledges the claim is based on absence of observed adverse events rather than systematic safety assessment. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this observation without raising safety concerns, noting the study was 'well performed.'

OpenEval R7 addresses the overarching mechanistic conclusion (C4-C7, C84, C121-C122) integrating multiple findings into a causal chain. Peer R2 partially overlaps by including C4 in the efficacy evaluation. Both support the overall conclusion, though OpenEval provides more comprehensive integration of the mechanistic pathway.

OpenEval R7 addresses the overarching mechanistic conclusion including C5-C7. Peer R4 addresses immune modulation findings including these claims. Both support the mechanistic link between immune modulation and reduced fibrosis, with OpenEval emphasizing the complete causal chain and peer reviewers focusing on specific immune cell and cytokine changes.

OpenEval R7 includes C84 (mechanistic pathway) as part of the overarching conclusion. Peer R5 includes C84 in the adoptive transfer evaluation. Both support the P2RX7-NLRP3-IL-18 pathway, with OpenEval integrating it into the broader causal chain and peer reviewers focusing on the adoptive transfer validation.

OpenEval R9 addresses the biological context (C89-C90) linking transcriptomic findings to established IPF biology. Peer R1 includes C89 as part of the transcriptomic evaluation. Both support the downregulation of the pathway in IPF and its biological significance.

OpenEval R11 addresses the mechanism of IL-18 selectivity (C99-C101) based on ELISA data and prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though this selectivity is implicitly accepted in peer R6 and R7.
